name: Edgewater Weeping Willow

location.address: Edgewater Park beach, by the Edgewater Beach House pedestrian bridge, Cleveland, OH

access: Free; Edgewater Park (Cleveland Metroparks Lakefront Reservation) is open to the public; the tree stands on the beach/lawn edge.
how_to_recognise: A lone, very broad weeping willow at the lakeshore edge of Edgewater Beach, beside the Edgewater Beach House footbridge; the most photographed single tree on the Cleveland lakefront.
photo_candidates: none fetched; a Commons/iNat search was not done. OSM node 9249098204 carries species:wikidata Q29994594.
verify_notes: Not ancient: a Metroparks historian dates it to about 1953 to 1958 (News 5 piece, which cites Cleveland Memory Project photos of a shrub-like tree at the spot in 1959 and 1969). Remarkable as Cleveland's most beloved tree: Metroparks lists it among its Ten Big Trees as a lakefront legend; News 5 quotes people proposing under it. Origin unknown; an ODNR forester speculates it grew from a branch washed ashore (speculation, labelled as such by the source). The land is landfill made in the 1950s from the straightening of the Cuyahoga River; the ground was Cleveland's, then ODNR's from 1978, Metroparks' since 2013. Weeping willows live 50 to 100 years per the article; lake storms can blow the top off. Pin is the OSM natural=tree node named Weeping Willow (tree-level coordinate; no aerial check done). Alive: Metroparks page of 2021 and News 5 piece (date not captured); lifecheck RECENT 2026-09-03 is nearby iNaturalist, not this tree. FLAG: a satire-looking blog (The Pierogi, 2026-03-20) says a Buc-ee's is planned at Edgewater with the willow marked for removal; unconfirmed and probably satire, no news source found, but check before writing. Height/girth: no source figure.

name: Lake View Cemetery Tulip Tree (Chapel Road)

location.address: Lake View Cemetery, 12316 Euclid Ave, Cleveland, OH (Section 1 or 6)
location.neighbourhood: Lake View Cemetery, University Circle / Cleveland Heights

access: Free; Lake View Cemetery is a public cemetery and arboretum (hours on lakeviewcemetery.com, not checked).
how_to_recognise: One of two tall tuliptrees the cemetery calls sentries, in Sections 1 and 6; the 1971 survey placed the big one on the west side of Chapel Road beside a large beech. Marked on the cemetery's 2026 map key.
verify_notes: Owner page: two grand tuliptrees, the tallest of the cemetery's seven Moses Cleaveland trees, stand in Sections 1 and 6 and are best seen looking up from the base. The 1971 Early Settlers survey (MCT 1946.089) calls it the largest tulip of the whole Moses Cleaveland group: 37 inches diameter in 1946, 39 inches in 1971 (girth about 311 cm from the 1971 diameter, measured 4.5 ft up, inches converted); it sits on Chapel Road, west side, near a large beech (1946.088, 30 to 32 inches). Which of the two tuliptrees 1946.089 is (Section 1 or 6) is not stated; section left open. Height: no source figure. Pin is the OSM Wade Memorial Chapel node, a reference point inside the cemetery, NOT the tree: the owner publishes sections and a keyed map PDF (lakeviewcemetery2026.pdf) but no coordinates. Age: a 'Moses Cleaveland tree' is one believed to predate 1796 (the 1946 survey qualified trees by trunk diameter); the age is the survey's belief, not a ring count, so age_min 230 only and age_max is a broad bound, not a source figure. Alive: owner page names it as present now; lifecheck RECENT 2026-03-11 (nearby iNaturalist, not the tree). Two sources: owner plus Freshwater Cleveland (2021) on the Early Settlers Association survey.
